I found no claims to flag. Every claim in the document is backed by the record, and the single went_wrong item isn't one its field excludes.

- **Root cause:** It is Code-Fix's reading of the source code (F1), and the document says plainly that F1 is unverified and that nothing ran it.
- **Causal chain:** The parts not taken from F1 match the record: the deploy that moved the categoriser model from v1 to v2 (P2), that change's diff (D1), and the configuration at the running revision (S1). It also matches the count of replicas on that revision (T10) and the confirmed rollback (M1, T20, T21).
- **Ruling out the earlier deploy (P1):** This holds up. The 361 minutes of metrics reach back to about 20:10 on 11 November, before P1 went out at 22:05:10. The onset was placed at 02:05 (T6).
- **Contributing factors:** The "no check was seen" and "no staged rollout seen" claims fit the record, which holds no such check or rollout.
- **Went wrong:** That nobody was paged is something the record itself calls a finding of its own.

I didn't judge the action items or the "had it been otherwise" what-ifs.

supported.quote: Model v2 looks words up exactly as it is given them, against a vocabulary built from titles that were already lowercased. The shop's `categorise` passes `title.split()` to `predict` without lowercasing it, a step v1 does itself inside `predict`. Under v2, any capitalised word in a purchase title missed the vocabulary, so the purchase was filed under "General" with `confident=False`. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.

Switching the shop to a newer model for sorting purchases into categories likely left capitalised words in product titles unrecognised: the new model only knows lowercase words, and the shop passed titles on without lowercasing them.

If automatic sync is turned back on, or the service is deployed again, while the repository still sets the categoriser to v2, the new model could come back and many purchases could again be filed without a confident category.
The shop stopped confidently categorising many shoppers' purchases
Many shoppers' purchases were no longer filed confidently under a category, while failed requests stayed within their normal variation.
rows: Rise above baseline: none beyond its normal variation

supported.quote: Deploy P2 at {P2.1} changed categoriser.model in deploy/values-production.yaml from v1 to v2. That is the only file the diff D1 lists, and S1 shows v2 set at the running revision.
The production categoriser had been switched from model v1 to model v2.
As of {T10.1}, all {T10.2} replicas ran that revision, and rolling the service back off it put things right (M1).
The metrics read reach back before it and show the service healthy until the onset at {T6.2}, and rolling back to that revision was confirmed to bring the service back to normal.
With v2 loaded (S1), purchase titles with capitalised words likely stopped matching the model's lowercase vocabulary, so those purchases fell to the general category without a confident filing.

No check was seen that runs a new categoriser model against mixed-case purchase titles and compares its confident share with the current model's before the config change ships. According to Code-Fix, the existing v2 tests used only words that were already lowercase.
The model switch went out as a plain config change to the whole deployment. No staged rollout and no gate on the confidence series were seen.
Nobody was paged: the alert was not linked to any on-call incident, so no person was brought in while Argus handled it.
